system_description.narrative_title: China–West economic-security decoupling and supply-chain contest
system_description.narrative_summary: News in this window coalesce around an intensifying strategic competition in which economic policy, technology controls and corporate repositioning are reshaping cross-border flows between China and Western actors. As an open system, actors (states, firms, investors, supply chains, regulators) exchange goods, capital, technology and information while policies and market reactions create reinforcing and balancing feedbacks (export controls, investment curbs, market access approvals, firm relocations). Key levers are regulatory measures, critical-materials access, corporate investment choices and political signalling from leadership meetings and plenum decisions, producing dynamic, multi-directional adjustments across the system.
system_description.scope: State actors (China, US, EU, Japan, Taiwan), multinational firms (tech, finance, auto, pharma), supply chains (semiconductors, batteries, rare earths), capital and investment flows, regulatory and trade policy instruments, market demand shocks and geopolitical signalling events.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic order (international trade, finance and security architecture)
adjacent_subsystems: Global technology and semiconductor supply chains
Asia‑Pacific regional security (Taiwan, maritime grey‑zone tactics)
Critical minerals and energy commodity markets (rare earths, batteries)

variables.name: Export Control Stringency
variables.description: Measures the restrictiveness and scope of export-control measures applied to goods, technologies and services crossing borders.

variables.name: Investment Screening Intensity
variables.description: Measures how aggressively cross-border investment is reviewed, restricted or conditioned by policy and administrative processes.

variables.name: Regulatory Uncertainty
variables.description: Measures perceived unpredictability and variance in regulatory outcomes affecting cross-border commercial activity.

variables.name: Institutional Cooperation Level
variables.description: Measures the degree of formal regulatory and policy cooperation across jurisdictions relevant to economic and security issues.

variables.name: Cross-border Capital Flow Volume
variables.description: Measures the rate and magnitude of financial capital moving across borders for investment, deposits and transactions.

variables.name: Supply Chain Concentration
variables.description: Measures the degree to which critical inputs and production stages are concentrated among a small set of suppliers or locations.

variables.name: Critical Materials Supply Risk
variables.description: Measures the vulnerability of access to essential raw materials based on availability, substitutability and market dynamics.

variables.name: Firm Reconfiguration Rate
variables.description: Measures the speed and frequency with which firms relocate, restructure or change sourcing and production footprints.

variables.name: Technology Transfer Rate
variables.description: Measures the pace at which technologies, know‑how and intellectual property move between actors and jurisdictions.

variables.name: Foreign Production Share
variables.description: Measures the proportion of production capacity or output located outside domestic jurisdiction(s) for a given set of industries.

variables.name: Corporate Foreign Market Exposure
variables.description: Measures firms' revenue, asset and operational dependence on external markets and customer bases.

variables.name: Market Demand Volatility
variables.description: Measures short- and medium-term variability in consumer and enterprise demand across relevant markets.

variables.name: Innovation Diffusion Rate
variables.description: Measures how quickly new products, processes and technologies are adopted across firms and markets.

variables.name: Information Control Intensity
variables.description: Measures the level of constraints on information flows, data sharing and research collaboration across borders.

variables.name: Geopolitical Tension Level
variables.description: Measures the intensity of strategic and security frictions that influence economic and cross-border interactions.

variables.name: Skilled Talent Mobility Rate
variables.description: Measures the rate at which skilled workers and researchers move across jurisdictions for employment or study.

catalysts.title: Further US export-control tightening on Chinese tech
catalysts.description: Ongoing US measures and enforcement actions targeting Chinese devices and surveillance-related tech, increasing export-control scope and enforcement intensity.
catalysts.rationale: US blocks devices with Chinese-made surveillance chips; continued enforcement signals further tightening.

catalysts.title: Finalization of US rules on sensitive China investment
catalysts.description: The US Treasury's proposed tighter rules on investing in sensitive Chinese tech move toward finalization, raising screening and restrictions on transactions.
catalysts.rationale: US Treasury proposes tighter investing rules; China urges halt to outbound-investment curbs.

catalysts.title: Acceleration of Chinese firms' overseas capacity investment
catalysts.description: Chinese manufacturers and battery firms accelerate building production overseas (e.g., BYD in Brazil) to mitigate Western barriers and market risk.
catalysts.rationale: BYD doubling Brazil capacity; battery makers racing to invest abroad to avoid western barriers.

catalysts.title: TSMC and peers seek non‑China equipment/suppliers
catalysts.description: Major chipmakers pursue equipment and supplier alternatives to reduce dependency on China-dominated rare‑earth and materials supply chains.
catalysts.rationale: TSMC seeks factory‑equipment alternatives to thwart China's rare earths grip.

catalysts.title: Near-term rare-earth squeeze risk for Japan
catalysts.description: Reports that Japan may run short of critical rare earths as China tightens supply, risking near-term production disruptions and strategic responses.
catalysts.rationale: Japan ‘months’ from running out of critical rare earth as China squeezes supply.

catalysts.title: EU‑China talks to address 'China Shock 2.0'
catalysts.description: EU ministers' pledged talks with Beijing to manage economic shock could produce coordinated policy responses or eased frictions depending on outcomes.
catalysts.rationale: EU ministers vow to tackle 'China Shock 2.0' through talks with Beijing.

catalysts.title: Increased grey‑zone pressure around Taiwan and allies
catalysts.description: China's stepped-up militia and grey‑zone tactics around Taiwan and allied states continue, raising strategic friction and business risk.
catalysts.rationale: China uses militia boats and grey‑zone tactics to isolate Taiwan and punish allies.

catalysts.title: Foreign banks' expanded access to Chinese markets
catalysts.description: Approvals like Citi's securities venture signal continued, incremental opening for foreign financial firms in China, affecting capital flows and cooperation.
catalysts.rationale: Citi wins approval for China securities business, indicating further foreign financial entry potential.
